status: Read-only bounded API plan; no production edits or new public API implemented.
decision: Add only a geometry-free consumer wrapper over existing focus_scope and scoped Bubble publication. Parent accepted the no-flags method shape.

api.signature: pub fn command_scope<C: Copy + 'static, R>(&mut self, owner: Id, table: &'static [Binding<C>], render: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui<'_>) -> R) -> R
implementation_sequence: Invoke render exactly once with the same Ui, preserving clipping, full area, layer, identity and focus bounds.
Publish existing ui.publish_scope_bindings(ScopeId::new(owner), owner, StateFlags::empty(), table) while still inside that real focus scope.
Return render result; reuse existing FocusScopeGuard restoration. Do not register a control or region for scope owner.
api.consumer_domain: Drain Intent::Binding(action) from cx.intents(owner), map Binding::command(the_same_table, action) into the application-owned Copy enum, then handle typed commands outside the immutable intent borrow. Return Response::changed/consumed only for an action actually handled; decline with Response::ignored to preserve outer/global fallback.
api.configuration: Use one stable container owner distinct from child component IDs and one static typed table shared between update and draw. Select an empty static slice when domain availability disables commands; no flags argument or implicit DISABLED/BUSY eligibility system.
api.remapping: Existing KeyMap::remap_component/remove_component(owner, action) already controls effective scoped chords through component_binding. Retain those contracts.
invariants: No input dispatch, domain effect, component update, or measurement in drawing/publication.
No new input stack, scope resolver, Capture phase, raw geometry, buffer painting, global-modal flag, or invisible focus control.
No scope action without an actual focused descendant in the current top layer; empty/no-focus modal must block background scopes.
Use stable unique owner IDs. Existing registration suppression prevents inert/reference content from publishing live scope bindings.
Existing global Capture and Bubble behavior remains unchanged; callers must remove route-local global entries when adopting scope ownership.

source_evidence.evidence: focus_scope creates the existing Normal scope, uses existing RAII guard and preserves Ui context.
publish_scope_bindings checks registration suppression/current scope layer, publishes typed descriptors and records existing ScopedBubbleBinding.
A public component-author publication bridge already exists; consumer wrapper must not reimplement it.
Owner-bound before_typing and global Capture occur before focused component dispatch. An app-global cockpit i/x action therefore bypasses an open PropsList modal.
Focused update runs first; scoped Bubble follows only when declined. Input layer/focus is rechecked before and after each scope callback. Global Bubble remains unscoped afterward.
Scope candidates require current focused entry on top layer and descendant scope membership; inner depth wins and bindings are revalidated against remapping/current scope.
Existing Binding<C>, Binding::command, component_binding and ScopedBubbleBinding supply typed action conversion and current descriptor state.
Modal closure saves restoration target; presentation reconciles against real current focus ring. Scope wrapper must not alter focus restoration.
An existing consumer already wraps a real detail scope and publishes scoped Bubble bindings through author API.
Frozen routing delivers to an open layer before route commands; unhandled modal keys are consumed rather than falling into background cockpit.
PropsList handles navigation/copy first; actual actions/close and Tab/ShiftTab/Esc follow; all other keys are consumed by modal.
Without a modal, cockpit handles log-owned keys and viewport first, then bare i/x domain commands. Scope migration must respect the log overlay/content context.
Current cockpit i/x/d/t are app-global Capture entries. i toggles info, and x opens cancel under an already-open info modal; removing only rendering plates cannot fix this routing.

application_red_green.red: Keep an unchanged real Jackin App/CLI regression that opens info then presses i/x and asserts info remains open, no cancel dialog/background action and unchanged relevant frame. Current app-global Capture path should fail.
application_red_green.green: After new wrapper adoption around actually rendered cockpit content, remove corresponding global route-local keymap entries and map typed scoped intents to existing domain handlers. The same App/CLI test must pass and frozen paired capture must agree.
application_red_green.separate_scope: The wrapper increment alone intentionally does not fix every current application global binding or establish baseline parity; d/t/build-log/cockpit quit/help precedence must be inventoried and migrated separately where frozen requires. Do not silently blanket-block all global commands in runtime.

adoption_dependency.baseline: CockpitScreen::enter/primary_focus selects real RAIL (cockpit.rs:556-562); draw registers its rendered rail at1002 through ctx.control(..., disabled=false), which actually registers a focus-ring entry (ctx.rs:335-343). StepRail.selectable(false) suppresses selection mechanics and its own focus styling, not this screen-owned real rail focus target.
adoption_dependency.candidate: Shared Steps::draw currently maps navigable=false to ClickOnly (steps.rs:686-693); it supplies no focus-ring entry. Current private cockpit painters do not establish equivalent shared focused descendants.
adoption_dependency.required: Before using command_scope for cockpit i/x, render a genuine shared focusable control matching frozen RAIL, or separately review a Steps contract that decouples focusability from navigation and matches frozen appearance. Never add a dummy one-cell/focus-only control, whole-app callback, or no-focus route fallback as a workaround.
adoption_dependency.appearance: Frozen nonselectable rail does not show selectable-row focus styling. Any real shared focusability adapter must preserve both keyboard ownership and visible baseline focus behavior.
